source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: All selected public labels match original source records. Complete verse records, including annotations, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the opening lament, female personification, and reversal from princess to forced labor.
verses.before: How she sits alone, the city once full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations. A princess among the provinces has become forced labor.
verses.after: How she sits alone, the city once full of people! She has become like a widow, once great among the nations. A princess among the provinces has been put to forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: How she sits alone, the city once full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations. A princess among the provinces has become forced labor.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled weeping, lovers/friends, and the comfort refrain.
verses.before: She weeps bitterly in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. She has no comforter among all her lovers. All her companions have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
verses.after: She weeps and weeps in the night, tears running down her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: She weeps bitterly in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. She has no comforter among all her lovers. All her companions have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ambiguous relation of affliction to exile and the trapped-space image.
verses.before: Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh servitude. She dwells among the nations and finds no rest. All her pursuers overtook her in narrow places.
verses.after: Judah has gone into exile through affliction and harsh servitude. She lives among the nations but finds no resting place. All her pursuers overtake her in the narrow places.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh servitude. She dwells among the nations and finds no rest. All her pursuers overtook her in narrow places.

verses.rationale: Preserves personified roads, religious gathering, and specific virgin term.
verses.before: The roads to Zion mourn because no one comes to the appointed festival. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan. Her young women grieve, and she herself is bitter.
verses.after: The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to the appointed feast. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan. Her virgins grieve, and she herself is bitter.
verses.tsw_comparator: The roads to Zion mourn because no one comes to the appointed festival. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan. Her young women grieve, and she herself is bitter.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit divine agency and children's captivity without adding a moral rationale beyond the text.
verses.before: Her adversaries have become the head; her enemies are at ease, for the LORD has afflicted her because of the multitude of her transgressions. Her little children have gone into captivity before the adversary.
verses.after: Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. The **LORD** has made her suffer for her many rebellions. Her little children have gone captive before the enemy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her adversaries have become the head; her enemies are at ease, for the LORD has afflicted her because of the multitude of her transgressions. Her little children have gone into captivity before the adversary.

verses.rationale: Follows the read from-daughter form and retains exhausted deer imagery.
verses.before: All splendor has departed from daughter Zion. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they go without strength before the pursuer.
verses.after: All her splendor has departed from daughter Zion. Her officials have become like deer that find no pasture. Without strength they walk before the pursuer.
verses.tsw_comparator: All splendor has departed from daughter Zion. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they go without strength before the pursuer.

verses.rationale: Preserves memory of former treasures and the enemy's derision.
verses.before: Jerusalem remembers, in the days of her affliction and wandering, all her precious things that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the hand of the adversary and there was no one to help her, the adversaries saw her and laughed at her downfall.
verses.after: In her days of affliction and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all her treasures from long ago. When her people fell into the enemy's hand, there was no one to help her. Her enemies saw her and laughed at her downfall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jerusalem remembers, in the days of her affliction and wandering, all her precious things that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the hand of the adversary and there was no one to help her, the adversaries saw her and laughed at her downfall.

verses.rationale: Keeps impurity and exposed nakedness as the poem's imagery, with a note distinguishing it from an endorsement of humiliation.
verses.before: Jerusalem sinned greatly; so she has become an impurity. Everyone who honored her despise her because they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away.
verses.after: Jerusalem has sinned grievously; so she has become unclean. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She too groans and turns away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jerusalem sinned greatly; therefore she has become an impurity. All who honored her despise her because they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away.

verses.rationale: Marks the first-person interruption and preserves the recurring absent comforter.
verses.before: Her uncleanness was in her skirts; she did not remember her end. She fell astonishingly; there is no one to comfort her. “See, O LORD, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself.”
verses.after: Her uncleanness is on her skirts; she gave no thought to her end. Her fall was astonishing; no one comforts her. “Look, **LORD**, at my affliction, for the enemy has made himself great!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Her uncleanness was in her skirts; she did not remember her end. She fell astonishingly; there is no one to comfort her. “See, O LORD, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself.”

verses.rationale: Retains the shift to addressing God and the sanctuary's violation.
verses.before: The adversary has spread his hand over all her precious things. She has seen nations enter her sanctuary, those whom you commanded not to enter your assembly.
verses.after: The enemy stretched out his hand over all her treasures. She saw nations enter her sanctuary, those you commanded not to enter your assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The adversary has spread his hand over all her precious things. She has seen nations enter her sanctuary, those whom you commanded not to enter your assembly.

verses.rationale: Follows the read treasures form and marks the city's renewed speech.
verses.before: All her people groan as they seek bread. They give their precious things for food to restore their lives. “See, O LORD, and look, for I have become despised.”
verses.after: All her people groan, searching for bread. They trade their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. “Look, **LORD**, and see: I have become despised.
verses.tsw_comparator: All her people groan as they seek bread. They give their precious things for food to restore their lives. “See, O LORD, and look, for I have become despised.”

verses.rationale: Uses the rhetorical-question reading of the difficult opening and retains divine affliction.
verses.before: Is it nothing to you, everyone who pass by? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, which was dealt to me, with which the LORD afflicted me on the day of his fierce anger.
verses.after: Does this mean nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see whether any pain is like my pain, like what has been done to me, what the **LORD** inflicted on the day of his burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is it nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, which was dealt to me, with which the LORD afflicted me on the day of his fierce anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps fire, bones, net, and the repeated divine actions rather than flattening them into distress.
verses.before: From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it prevailed over them. He spread a net for my feet; he turned me back. He made me desolate, faint all day long.
verses.after: From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it mastered them. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He left me desolate, sick all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it prevailed over them. He spread a net for my feet; he turned me back. He made me desolate, faint all day long.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult bound-yoke reading and the Lord distinct from **LORD**.
verses.before: The yoke of my transgressions was bound by his hand; they were intertwined and came up upon my neck. He made my strength fail. The Lord gave me into hands against which I cannot stand.
verses.after: The yoke of my rebellions was bound by his hand; woven together, they rose onto my neck. He made my strength fail. The Lord handed me over to those I cannot withstand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The yoke of my transgressions was bound by his hand; they were intertwined and came up upon my neck. He made my strength fail. The Lord gave me into hands against which I cannot stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the appointed-assembly reversal and bodily winepress violence.
verses.before: The Lord rejected all my mighty ones in my midst. He summoned an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden the winepress for virgin daughter Judah.
verses.after: The Lord has cast aside all the mighty men within me. He called an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden virgin daughter Judah as grapes in a winepress.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord rejected all my mighty ones in my midst. He summoned an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden the winepress for virgin daughter Judah.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated eye and lack of life-restoring comfort.
verses.before: For these things I weep; my eye, my eye pours down water, because a comforter is far from me, one who would restore my life. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.
verses.after: For these things I weep; my eye, my eye pours out water. Far from me is a comforter, one who could restore my life. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For these things I weep; my eye, my eye pours down water, because a comforter is far from me, one who would restore my life. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.

verses.rationale: Marks the narrative interruption and preserves commanded hostility.
verses.before: Zion stretches out her hands; there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him become his adversaries. Jerusalem has become an impurity among them.
verses.after: Zion spreads out her hands; no one comforts her. The **LORD** has commanded that Jacob's neighbors become his foes. Jerusalem has become unclean among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zion stretches out her hands; there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him become his adversaries. Jerusalem has become an impurity among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps confession and appeal together without allowing one to cancel the other.
verses.before: The LORD is righteous, for I rebelled against his mouth. Hear, all you peoples, and see my pain: my young women and my young men have gone into captivity.
verses.after: “The **LORD** is righteous, for I rebelled against his command. Listen, all you peoples, and see my pain. My virgins and young men have gone into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is righteous, for I rebelled against his mouth. Hear, all you peoples, and see my pain: my young women and my young men have gone into captivity.

verses.rationale: Preserves failed allies and leaders dying in their search for sustenance.
verses.before: I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while seeking food for themselves to restore their lives.
verses.after: I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and elders died in the city as they searched for food to keep themselves alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while seeking food for themselves to restore their lives.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily turmoil and the source's qualified like-death phrase.
verses.before: See, O LORD, for I am in distress. My inward parts churn; my heart is overturned within me, for I have greatly rebelled. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.
verses.after: Look, **LORD**, how distressed I am! My insides churn; my heart turns over within me, for I have rebelled deeply. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, it is like death.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, O LORD, for I am in distress. My inward parts churn; my heart is overturned within me, for I have greatly rebelled. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.

verses.rationale: Uses a petition reading for the announced day and preserves the request for others to share her fate.
verses.before: They have heard that I groan; there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my disaster; they rejoice because you have done it. Bring the day you proclaimed, and let them become like me.
verses.after: They hear my groaning, but no one comforts me. All my enemies hear of my disaster; they rejoice that you have done it. Bring the day you announced, and let them become like me.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have heard that I groan; there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my disaster; they rejoice because you have done it. Bring the day you proclaimed, and let them become like me.

verses.rationale: Retains retribution petition and exhausted closing without a consoling addition.
verses.before: Let all their evil come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my transgressions. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.
verses.after: Let all their evil come before you. Deal with them as you dealt with me for all my rebellions. My groans are many, and my heart is sick.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let all their evil come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my transgressions. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.

verses.rationale: Preserves cloud, downward casting, and footstool imagery.
verses.before: How the Lord, in his anger, has covered daughter Zion with a cloud! He has cast the splendor of Israel from heaven to earth and has not remembered his footstool on the day of his anger.
verses.after: How the Lord has covered daughter Zion with the cloud of his anger! He hurled Israel's splendor from heaven to earth. On the day of his anger he did not remember his footstool.
verses.tsw_comparator: How the Lord, in his anger, has covered daughter Zion with a cloud! He has cast the splendor of Israel from heaven to earth and has not remembered his footstool on the day of his anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps swallowing and lack of pity with royal profanation.
verses.before: The Lord swallowed up without compassion all the dwellings of Jacob. In his wrath he tore down the strongholds of daughter Judah; he brought kingdom and princes down to the ground and profaned them.
verses.after: The Lord swallowed up without pity all Jacob's dwellings. In his fury he tore down daughter Judah's fortresses. He brought them to the ground, profaning the kingdom and its rulers.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord swallowed up without compassion all the dwellings of Jacob. In his wrath he tore down the strongholds of daughter Judah; he brought kingdom and princes down to the ground and profaned them.

verses.rationale: Retains horn and withdrawn hand as bodily images of lost strength and protection.
verses.before: In fierce anger he cut off every horn of Israel. He drew back his right hand before the enemy and burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes all around.
verses.after: In burning anger he cut off every horn of Israel. He drew back his right hand in the face of the enemy. He burned in Jacob like a flaming fire, devouring all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: In fierce anger he cut off every horn of Israel. He drew back his right hand before the enemy and burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes all around.

verses.rationale: Keeps God like an enemy and the full agency of killing.
verses.before: He bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand stood like an adversary. He killed everyone who were pleasing to the eye. In the tent of daughter Zion he poured out his fury like fire.
verses.after: He drew his bow like an enemy, his right hand poised like a foe. He killed all that delighted the eye. In daughter Zion's tent he poured out his wrath like fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: He bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand stood like an adversary. He killed all who were pleasing to the eye. In the tent of daughter Zion he poured out his fury like fire.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated swallowing and paired sounds of grief.
verses.before: The Lord has become like an enemy; he swallowed up Israel. He swallowed all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He multiplied mourning and lamentation in daughter Judah.
verses.after: The Lord has become like an enemy. He swallowed up Israel, swallowed all her palaces, destroyed her fortresses. He multiplied mourning and moaning in daughter Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord has become like an enemy; he swallowed up Israel. He swallowed all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He multiplied mourning and lamentation in daughter Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult garden comparison and the distinct divine name.
verses.before: He violently stripped away his shelter as if it were a garden; he destroyed his appointed meeting place. The LORD caused appointed festival and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, and in the indignation of his anger he rejected king and priest.
verses.after: He tore away his shelter as if it were a garden; he destroyed his appointed meeting place. The **LORD** made feast and Sabbath forgotten in Zion; in his fierce anger he spurned king and priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: He violently stripped away his shelter as though it were a garden; he destroyed his appointed meeting place. The LORD caused appointed festival and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, and in the indignation of his anger he rejected king and priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps Lord/**LORD** distinction and the bitter festival comparison.
verses.before: The Lord rejected his altar and disowned his sanctuary. He handed the walls of her palaces over to the enemy. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a day of appointed festival.
verses.after: The Lord rejected his altar, repudiated his sanctuary. He handed the walls of her palaces over to the enemy. They raised their voices in the **LORD**'s house as on a feast day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord rejected his altar and disowned his sanctuary. He handed the walls of her palaces over to the enemy. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a day of appointed festival.

verses.rationale: Preserves deliberate measured destruction and personified fortifications.
verses.before: The LORD determined to destroy the wall of daughter Zion. He stretched out the measuring line and did not withdraw his hand from swallowing up. He caused rampart and wall to mourn; together they languish.
verses.after: The **LORD** planned to destroy daughter Zion's wall. He stretched out a measuring line and did not draw back his destroying hand. He made rampart and wall mourn; together they languished.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD determined to destroy the wall of daughter Zion. He stretched out the measuring line and did not withdraw his hand from swallowing up. He caused rampart and wall to mourn; together they languish.

verses.rationale: Keeps the loss of civic, instructional, and prophetic resources distinct.
verses.before: Her gates have sunk into the ground; he destroyed and shattered her bars. Her king and princes are among the nations; there is no instruction. Her prophets also find no vision from the LORD.
verses.after: Her gates sank into the ground; he destroyed and broke their bars. Her king and officials are among the nations. There is no instruction; even her prophets find no vision from the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her gates have sunk into the ground; he destroyed and shattered her bars. Her king and princes are among the nations; there is no instruction. Her prophets also find no vision from the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves age/gender groups and bodily mourning gestures.
verses.before: The elders of daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence. They throw dust upon their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.
verses.after: Daughter Zion's elders sit on the ground in silence. They throw dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. Jerusalem's virgins bow their heads to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence. They throw dust upon their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains liver as an ancient bodily image and children's collapse.
verses.before: My eyes are spent with tears; my inward parts churn. My liver is poured out on the ground because of the breaking of daughter my people, as child and infant faint in the streets of the city.
verses.after: My eyes are spent with tears; my insides churn. My liver is poured out on the ground because my people are shattered, because children and nursing infants faint in the town's squares.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eyes are spent with tears; my inward parts churn. My liver is poured out on the ground because of the breaking of daughter my people, as child and infant faint in the streets of the city.

verses.rationale: Keeps the children's question and the outpouring of life without euphemism.
verses.before: They say to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives pour out upon their mothers’ bosoms.
verses.after: They ask their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” They faint like the wounded in the city squares, their lives pouring away in their mothers' arms.
verses.tsw_comparator: They say to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives pour out upon their mothers’ bosoms.

verses.rationale: Preserves the search for comparison and the unanswered question.
verses.before: What can I testify to you? To what can I compare you, daughter Jerusalem? What can I liken to you so that I may comfort you, virgin daughter Zion? For your breaking is as great as the sea. Who can heal you?
verses.after: What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, daughter Jerusalem? What can I set beside you to comfort you, virgin daughter Zion? Your breach is as vast as the sea. Who can heal you?
verses.tsw_comparator: What can I testify to you? To what can I compare you, daughter Jerusalem? What can I liken to you so that I may comfort you, virgin daughter Zion? For your breaking is as great as the sea. Who can heal you?

verses.rationale: Follows the read fortunes form and retains prophetic failure without adding a sermon.
verses.before: Your prophets saw for you empty and deceptive visions. They did not expose your guilt to turn back your captivity, but saw for you oracles of emptiness and misdirection.
verses.after: Your prophets saw empty and hollow visions for you. They did not expose your guilt to restore your fortunes. They saw for you empty oracles that led you astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your prophets saw for you empty and deceptive visions. They did not expose your guilt to turn back your captivity, but saw for you oracles of emptiness and misdirection.

verses.rationale: Keeps mocking gestures and the city's former titles in the taunt.
verses.before: Everyone who pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
verses.after: All who pass by clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city they called perfect in beauty, the joy of the whole earth?”
verses.tsw_comparator: All who pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”

verses.rationale: Preserves enemy triumph and the doubled arrival/seeing claim.
verses.before: All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and gnash their teeth. They say, “We have swallowed her! Surely this is the day we waited for; we have found it, we have seen it.”
verses.after: All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and grind their teeth. They say, “We have swallowed her! This is the day we waited for. We have reached it; we have seen it!”
verses.tsw_comparator: All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and gnash their teeth. They say, “We have swallowed her! Surely this is the day we waited for; we have found it, we have seen it.”

verses.rationale: Retains fulfilled intention and the enemy's raised horn against Israel's cut horns.
verses.before: The LORD has done what he planned; he fulfilled his word that he commanded from days of old. He tore down and did not have compassion. He made the enemy rejoice over you and raised the horn of your adversaries.
verses.after: The **LORD** has done what he planned, fulfilled the word he commanded long ago. He tore down without pity; he let the enemy rejoice over you and raised the horn of your foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has done what he planned; he fulfilled his word that he commanded from days of old. He tore down and did not have compassion. He made the enemy rejoice over you and raised the horn of your adversaries.

verses.rationale: Keeps the abrupt address to the wall and literal eye image, explained in a note.
verses.before: Their heart cried out to the Lord. O wall of daughter Zion, let tears run down like a torrent day and night. Give yourself no relief; let the pupil of your eye have no rest.
verses.after: Their hearts cry out to the Lord. Wall of daughter Zion, let tears flow like a torrent day and night. Give yourself no rest; let the pupil of your eye never cease.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their heart cried out to the Lord. O wall of daughter Zion, let tears run down like a torrent day and night. Give yourself no relief; let the pupil of your eye have no rest.

verses.rationale: Preserves night watches, water image, and petition for starving children.
verses.before: Rise! Cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift your hands toward him for the lives of your children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.
verses.after: Rise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of each watch. Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to him for your children's lives; they faint from hunger at every street corner.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise! Cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift your hands toward him for the lives of your children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct protest, cannibalism, and both divine designations without sensational detail.
verses.before: See, O LORD, and look: to whom have you done this? Should women eat their own fruit, the children they have cared for? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.after: “Look, **LORD**, and see: whom have you treated this way? Should women eat their own offspring, the children they have nurtured? Should priest and prophet be killed in the Lord's sanctuary?
verses.tsw_comparator: See, O LORD, and look: to whom have you done this? Should women eat their own fruit, the children they have cared for? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

verses.rationale: Retains the direct accusation and repeated killing verbs.
verses.before: Young and old lie on the ground in the streets. My young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You killed them on the day of your anger; you slaughtered without compassion.
verses.after: Young and old lie on the ground in the streets. My virgins and young men have fallen by the sword. You killed them on the day of your anger; you slaughtered without pity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Young and old lie on the ground in the streets. My young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You killed them on the day of your anger; you slaughtered without compassion.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inverted feast and maternal closing grief.
verses.before: You summoned, as on a festival day, my terrors from all around. On the day of the LORD’s anger there was no one who escaped or survived. Those whom I cared for and raised, my enemy consumed.
verses.after: You summoned my terrors from every side as though to a feast day. On the day of the **LORD**'s anger there was no fugitive or survivor. Those I nurtured and raised, my enemy consumed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You summoned, as on a festival day, my terrors from all around. On the day of the LORD’s anger there was no one who escaped or survived. Those whom I cared for and raised, my enemy consumed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the male speaker and unnamed he at the opening.
verses.before: I am the one who has seen affliction under the rod of the LORD’s wrath.
verses.after: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the one who has seen affliction under the rod of the LORD’s wrath.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine compulsion and negative contrast.
verses.before: The LORD has driven me and brought me into darkness and not into light.
verses.after: He led me and made me walk in darkness, without light.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has driven me and brought me into darkness and not into light.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated hostile action and duration.
verses.before: Surely the LORD turns a hand against me, again and again all the day long.
verses.after: Against me he turns his hand again and again, all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely the LORD turns a hand against me, again and again all the day long.

verses.rationale: Retains concrete bodily damage.
verses.before: The LORD has made my flesh and my skin waste away; the LORD has broken my bones.
verses.after: He wore away my flesh and skin; he broke my bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has made my flesh and my skin waste away; the LORD has broken my bones.

verses.rationale: Unpacks the building-against image while keeping bitter encirclement.
verses.before: The LORD has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
verses.after: He built siegeworks against me, surrounding me with bitterness and hardship.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.

verses.rationale: Preserves the burial-like dwelling comparison.
verses.before: The LORD has made me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.
verses.after: He made me live in dark places, like those long dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has made me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.

verses.rationale: Keeps confinement and the stated material of the bond.
verses.before: The LORD has walled me in so that I cannot escape; the LORD has made my chains heavy.
verses.after: He walled me in so I cannot escape; he made my bronze chain heavy.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has walled me in so that I cannot escape; the LORD has made my chains heavy.

verses.rationale: Retains blocked prayer without an immediate reassurance.
verses.before: Even when I cry and call for help, the LORD shuts out my prayer.
verses.after: Even when I cry out and plead, he shuts out my prayer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even when I cry and call for help, the LORD shuts out my prayer.

verses.rationale: Keeps both obstruction and distortion.
verses.before: The LORD has blocked my ways with hewn stones; the LORD has made my paths crooked.
verses.after: He blocked my roads with cut stone and twisted my paths.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has blocked my ways with hewn stones; the LORD has made my paths crooked.

verses.rationale: Preserves God as predator and follows the read lion form.
verses.before: The LORD is to me like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in hiding.
verses.after: He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hiding.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is to me like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in hiding.

verses.rationale: Keeps the violent tearing and resulting isolation.
verses.before: The LORD turned aside my steps and tore me to pieces; the LORD has left me desolate.
verses.after: He forced me off my paths and tore me apart; he left me desolate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD turned aside my steps and tore me to pieces; the LORD has left me desolate.

verses.rationale: Retains the target image and deliberate positioning.
verses.before: The LORD bent the bow and set me as a target for the arrow.
verses.after: He drew his bow and set me up as a target for his arrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD bent the bow and set me as a target for the arrow.

verses.rationale: Preserves both ancient arrow metaphor and bodily organ, explained in vocabulary.
verses.before: The LORD drove into my kidneys the arrows of the LORD’s quiver.
verses.after: He drove the sons of his quiver into my kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD drove into my kidneys the arrows of the LORD’s quiver.

verses.rationale: Keeps my people rather than silently emending to all peoples.
verses.before: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their mocking song all day long.
verses.after: I became a laughingstock to all my people, the subject of their songs all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their mocking song all day long.

verses.rationale: Retains bitter eating/drinking and named plant.
verses.before: The LORD has filled me with bitterness; the LORD has made me drunk with wormwood.
verses.after: He filled me with bitter things and made me drink my fill of wormwood.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has filled me with bitterness; the LORD has made me drunk with wormwood.

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete humiliation without reducing it to sadness.
verses.before: The LORD has ground my teeth with gravel; the LORD has pressed me into the dust.
verses.after: He ground my teeth with gravel and pressed me into ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has ground my teeth with gravel; the LORD has pressed me into the dust.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sudden second-person turn and loss of remembered good.
verses.before: My whole being is deprived of peace; I have forgotten what well-being is.
verses.after: You have driven my life away from peace; I have forgotten what good is.
verses.tsw_comparator: My whole being is deprived of peace; I have forgotten what well-being is.

verses.rationale: Uses endurance for the disputed noun and keeps hope's named source.
verses.before: So I said, “My endurance has perished, and so has my hope from the LORD.”
verses.after: I said, “My endurance is gone, and so is my hope from the **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I said, “My endurance has perished, and so has my hope from the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Reads the opening as an appeal while noting possible recollection reading.
verses.before: Remember my affliction and my wandering— the wormwood and the gall!
verses.after: Remember my affliction and wandering, the wormwood and the poison.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember my affliction and my wandering— the wormwood and the gall!

verses.rationale: Follows the read sinking form and preserves repeated memory.
verses.before: My whole being remembers it and is bowed down within me.
verses.after: My soul remembers them again and again and sinks within me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My whole being remembers it and is bowed down within me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the turn dependent on remembered content rather than erasing prior suffering.
verses.before: But this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
verses.after: But this I bring back to mind, and so I have hope:
verses.tsw_comparator: But this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned first-person plural we, with the familiar alternative noted.
verses.before: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; the LORD’s mercies never come to an end;
verses.after: Through the **LORD**'s acts of steadfast love we have not come to an end, for his compassion has not run out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; the LORD’s mercies never come to an end;

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift to direct address and plural renewal.
verses.before: they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
verses.after: They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness!
verses.tsw_comparator: they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Retains portion as biblical vocabulary and inner speech.
verses.before: “The LORD is my portion,” says my whole being, “therefore I will hope in the LORD.”
verses.after: “The **LORD** is my portion,” my soul says, “so I will hope in him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD is my portion,” says my whole being, “therefore I will hope in the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps waiting/seeking parallelism without changing it to passive optimism.
verses.before: The LORD is good to people who wait for him, to the one who seeks him.
verses.after: The **LORD** is good to those who wait for him, to the person who seeks him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the one who seeks him.

verses.rationale: Retains salvation and quiet waiting as the poem states them.
verses.before: It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.
verses.after: It is good to wait quietly for the **LORD**'s salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves male noun, yoke, and life-stage image.
verses.before: It is good for a person to bear the yoke in youth.
verses.after: It is good for a man to carry a yoke in his youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is good for a person to bear the yoke in youth.

verses.rationale: Makes the implied divine agent explicit for readable pronouns; a self-assumed burden remains a noted alternative.
verses.before: Let them sit alone in silence when the LORD has laid it on them;
verses.after: Let him sit alone and be silent, for God has laid it on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them sit alone in silence when the LORD has laid it on them;

verses.rationale: Retains the tentative perhaps and extreme posture.
verses.before: let them put their mouth in the dust— perhaps there may yet be hope;
verses.after: Let him put his mouth in the dust— perhaps there is hope.
verses.tsw_comparator: let them put their mouth in the dust— perhaps there may yet be hope;

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult submission language in the lament's voice without turning it into advice to victims.
verses.before: let them give their cheek to the one who strikes, and let them be filled with insults.
verses.after: Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him have his fill of disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: let them give their cheek to the one who strikes, and let them be filled with insults.

verses.rationale: Preserves the brief assertion and Lord designation.
verses.before: For the Lord will not reject forever,
verses.after: For the Lord will not reject forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord will not reject forever,

verses.rationale: Keeps grief's divine agency together with compassion.
verses.before: but though he causes grief, he will have compassion according to the abundance of his steadfast love;
verses.after: Though he causes grief, he will show compassion according to his abundant steadfast love.
verses.tsw_comparator: but though he causes grief, he will have compassion according to the abundance of his steadfast love;

verses.rationale: Retains the heart idiom and the tension with preceding agency, explained in a note.
verses.before: for he does not afflict from his heart or grieve the children of humanity.
verses.after: For it is not from his heart that he afflicts or grieves human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he does not afflict from his heart or grieve the children of humanity.

verses.rationale: Lets the infinitive list continue across labels.
verses.before: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,
verses.after: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,
verses.tsw_comparator: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,

verses.rationale: Preserves justice and the divine title.
verses.before: to deny a person justice before the face of the Most High,
verses.after: to deny a man justice in the presence of the Most High,
verses.tsw_comparator: to deny a person justice before the face of the Most High,

verses.rationale: Uses the rhetorical-question reading and notes the approval-reading alternative.
verses.before: to subvert a person in a lawsuit— the Lord does not approve.
verses.after: to wrong someone in a lawsuit— does the Lord not see?
verses.tsw_comparator: to subvert a person in a lawsuit— the Lord does not approve.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical challenge to independent agency.
verses.before: Who has spoken and it happened, unless the Lord has commanded it?
verses.after: Who speaks and it happens unless the Lord has commanded it?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?

verses.rationale: Preserves the question and both outcomes without glossing disaster as moral evil.
verses.before: Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both calamity and good come?
verses.after: Do not disaster and good alike come from the mouth of the Most High?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both calamity and good come?

verses.rationale: Makes the punishment sense explicit while noting the compressed sins wording.
verses.before: Why should any living person complain about the punishment of their sins?
verses.after: Why should a living man complain about the consequences of his sins?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should any living person complain about the punishment of their sins?

verses.rationale: Preserves the turn to communal exhortation.
verses.before: Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the LORD.
verses.after: Let us examine and search our ways and return to the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps inward and bodily prayer together.
verses.before: Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven:
verses.after: Let us lift our hearts with our hands to God in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven:

verses.rationale: Preserves the unresolved accusation following confession.
verses.before: “We have rebelled and been stubborn, and you have not forgiven.”
verses.after: We have rebelled and defied you; you have not forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: “We have rebelled and been stubborn, and you have not forgiven.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct address and violent agency.
verses.before: You have wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you have killed without pity.
verses.after: You wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you killed without pity.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you have killed without pity.

verses.rationale: Retains the barrier-to-prayer image after the hopeful passage.
verses.before: You have wrapped yourself with a cloud so that prayer cannot pass through.
verses.after: You wrapped yourself in a cloud so no prayer could pass through.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have wrapped yourself with a cloud so that prayer cannot pass through.

verses.rationale: Preserves degrading paired nouns.
verses.before: You have made us scum and refuse among the peoples.
verses.after: You made us refuse and filth among the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have made us scum and refuse among the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps collective hostility and the mouth image.
verses.before: All our enemies open their mouths against us.
verses.after: All our enemies open their mouths against us.
verses.tsw_comparator: All our enemies open their mouths against us.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fourfold compressed calamity and sound pairing.
verses.before: Terror and pitfall have come upon us, ruin and destruction.
verses.after: Terror and pit have come upon us, devastation and destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Terror and pitfall have come upon us, ruin and destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps the individual voice reentering communal grief.
verses.before: My eyes flow with streams of tears because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
verses.after: My eye pours out streams of water because my people are shattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eyes flow with streams of tears because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unfinished sentence and repeated unceasing tears.
verses.before: My eyes will pour down without ceasing, without relief,
verses.after: My eye streams without stopping, without a moment's relief,
verses.tsw_comparator: My eyes will pour down without ceasing, without relief,

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional horizon without claiming it already happened.
verses.before: until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.
verses.after: until the **LORD** looks down and sees from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.

verses.rationale: Retains daughters and notes the ambiguous comparative/cause expression.
verses.before: My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
verses.after: What my eye sees torments my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.

verses.rationale: Keeps innocence claim and hunted-bird image.
verses.before: People who are my enemies without cause hunted me like a bird;
verses.after: Those who hated me without cause hunted me like a bird.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who are my enemies without cause hunted me like a bird;

verses.rationale: Reads the compressed destruction in a pit with stones directed at the speaker; note gives alternative sealing stone.
verses.before: they cast me alive into the pit and threw stones on me;
verses.after: They tried to end my life in a pit and threw stones at me.
verses.tsw_comparator: they cast me alive into the pit and threw stones on me;

verses.rationale: Preserves the submerged speaker and despairing quotation.
verses.before: water closed over my head; I said, “I am lost.”
verses.after: Water closed over my head. I said, “I am cut off!”
verses.tsw_comparator: water closed over my head; I said, “I am lost.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the named appeal and depth.
verses.before: I called on your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit;
verses.after: I called your name, **LORD**, from the deepest pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: I called on your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit;

verses.rationale: Retains remembered hearing and quoted plea, noting breathing/relief sense.
verses.before: you heard my voice: “Do not hide your ear from my sighing, from my cry for help.”
verses.after: You heard my voice: “Do not close your ear to my plea for relief, to my cry for help.”
verses.tsw_comparator: you heard my voice: “Do not hide your ear from my sighing, from my cry for help.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the remembered response in direct speech.
verses.before: You came near when I called on you; you said, “Do not fear!”
verses.after: You drew near when I called to you; you said, “Do not fear.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You came near when I called on you; you said, “Do not fear!”

verses.rationale: Preserves plural legal cases and redemption vocabulary.
verses.before: You have taken up my cause, O Lord; you have redeemed my life.
verses.after: Lord, you took up the cases concerning my life; you redeemed my life.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have taken up my cause, O Lord; you have redeemed my life.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine seeing and imperative legal petition.
verses.before: O LORD, you have seen the wrong done to me; judge my case.
verses.after: You have seen the wrong done to me, **LORD**; judge my case.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, you have seen the wrong done to me; judge my case.

verses.rationale: Retains both hostility terms and repeated all.
verses.before: You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
verses.after: You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing alongside the previous seeing and continuation into the next verse.
verses.before: You have heard their insults, O LORD, all their plots against me—
verses.after: You have heard their insults, **LORD**, all their plots against me,
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard their insults, O LORD, all their plots against me—

verses.rationale: Retains persistent hostile speech.
verses.before: the lips and thoughts of my attackers, all day long.
verses.after: the words of those who rise against me, their muttering against me all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: the lips and thoughts of my attackers, all day long.

verses.rationale: Preserves the whole-day posture pair and song motif.
verses.before: Look at them—sitting or rising; I am their mocking song.
verses.after: Look at them sitting and rising— I am their mocking song.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at them—sitting or rising; I am their mocking song.

verses.rationale: Keeps the retributive petition as a petition.
verses.before: You will repay them, O LORD, according to the work of their hands.
verses.after: Repay them, **LORD**, according to what their hands have done.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will repay them, O LORD, according to the work of their hands.

verses.rationale: Preserves the obscure covering image and notes its possible hardening sense.
verses.before: You will give them hardness of heart; your curse will be on them.
verses.after: Give them a covering over the heart; let your curse be on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will give them hardness of heart; your curse will be on them.

verses.rationale: Retains the severe ending and third-person divine name within direct prayer.
verses.before: You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.
verses.after: Pursue them in anger and destroy them from beneath the heavens of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the gold and scattered sanctuary imagery without deciding all referents in the text.
verses.before: How the gold has grown dim! How the fine gold has changed! The holy stones are poured out at the head of every street.
verses.after: How the gold has grown dim, the fine gold changed! The sacred stones lie scattered at every street corner.
verses.tsw_comparator: How the gold has grown dim! How the fine gold has changed! The holy stones are poured out at the head of every street.

verses.rationale: Preserves sons and the gold-to-pottery reversal.
verses.before: The precious children of Zion, weighed against fine gold— how they are now regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter’s hands!
verses.after: Zion's precious sons, worth their weight in pure gold— how they are treated as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands!
verses.tsw_comparator: The precious children of Zion, weighed against fine gold— how they are now regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter’s hands!

verses.rationale: Follows both read animal forms and retains the harsh poetic comparison, with cultural context in notes.
verses.before: Even jackals bare the breast and nurse their young, but daughter my people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
verses.after: Even jackals offer the breast and nurse their young. But my people have become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even jackals bare the breast and nurse their young, but daughter my people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete infant suffering and bread-breaking image.
verses.before: The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Little children ask for bread, but no one breaks it for them.
verses.after: The nursing infant's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Children ask for bread, but no one breaks it for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Little children ask for bread, but no one breaks it for them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the class reversal and embrace image.
verses.before: People who ate delicacies lie desolate in the streets. Those raised in scarlet embrace refuse heaps.
verses.after: Those who ate delicacies lie desolate in the streets. Those raised in scarlet embrace refuse heaps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who ate delicacies lie desolate in the streets. Those raised in scarlet embrace refuse heaps.

verses.rationale: Chooses punishment sense and retains the disputed hands phrase with alternatives noted.
verses.before: The guilt of daughter my people was greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment without hands laid upon it.
verses.after: My people's punishment is greater than Sodom's punishment. Sodom was overthrown in a moment, with no hands turned against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: The guilt of daughter my people was greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment without hands laid upon it.

verses.rationale: Keeps consecrated ones rather than deciding nobles, and preserves color/material comparisons with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Her consecrated ones were purer than snow, whiter than milk. Their bodies were more ruddy than coral; their form was like sapphire.
verses.after: Her consecrated ones were purer than snow, whiter than milk. Their bodies were ruddier than coral, their form like sapphire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her consecrated ones were purer than snow, whiter than milk. Their bodies were more ruddy than coral; their form was like sapphire.

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily contrast without racial interpretation.
verses.before: Their appearance is darker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled upon their bones; it has become dry like wood.
verses.after: Now their appearance is darker than soot; no one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin clings to their bones, dry as wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their appearance is darker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled upon their bones; it has become dry like wood.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shocking comparison and hunger-as-piercing image.
verses.before: Better were those pierced by the sword than those pierced by hunger, who waste away, struck through for lack of produce from the field.
verses.after: Better off are those killed by the sword than those killed by hunger. They waste away, pierced through for lack of the field's produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better were those pierced by the sword than those pierced by hunger, who waste away, struck through for lack of produce from the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps compassionate women and cannibalism together without blaming an inherent lack of care.
verses.before: The hands of compassionate women cooked their own children; they became their food in the breaking of daughter my people.
verses.after: The hands of compassionate women have cooked their own children. They became their food when my people were shattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hands of compassionate women cooked their own children; they became their food in the breaking of daughter my people.

verses.rationale: Retains wrath exhausted and fire consuming the city's base.
verses.before: The LORD spent his fury; he poured out his fierce anger. He kindled a fire in Zion that consumed her foundations.
verses.after: The **LORD** has spent his wrath, poured out his burning anger. He kindled a fire in Zion that consumed her foundations.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spent his fury; he poured out his fierce anger. He kindled a fire in Zion that consumed her foundations.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sweeping claim of incredulity rather than correcting it historically.
verses.before: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did any inhabitants of the world, that adversary and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.after: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did anyone living in the world, that foe and enemy could enter Jerusalem's gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did any inhabitants of the world, that adversary and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps leadership's specific bloodguilt and the causal fragment's relation to the fall.
verses.before: It was because of the sins of her prophets, the guilt of her priests, who shed within her the blood of the righteous.
verses.after: It was because of her prophets' sins and her priests' guilt: they shed the blood of the righteous within her.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was because of the sins of her prophets, the guilt of her priests, who shed within her the blood of the righteous.

verses.rationale: Preserves blindness, pollution, and forbidden contact without changing blood to metaphor.
verses.before: They wandered blind in the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.
verses.after: They staggered blindly through the streets, polluted with blood, so that no one could touch their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: They wandered blind in the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated exclusion and displacement, marking speakers minimally.
verses.before: “Turn away! Unclean!” people cried to them. “Turn away! Turn away! Do not touch!” So they fled and wandered. Among the nations it was said, “They will no longer stay here.”
verses.after: “Away! Unclean!” people cried at them. “Away, away! Do not touch!” When they fled and wandered, people among the nations said, “They may stay here no longer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Turn away! Unclean!” people cried to them. “Turn away! Turn away! Do not touch!” So they fled and wandered. Among the nations it was said, “They shall no longer stay here.”

verses.rationale: Retains the divine face/presence sense and parallels rejected leaders.
verses.before: The face of the LORD scattered them; he will no longer look upon them. No respect was shown to priests, and no favor to elders.
verses.after: The **LORD**'s presence scattered them; he will look on them no longer. Priests received no honor; elders received no favor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The face of the LORD scattered them; he will no longer look upon them. No respect was shown to priests, and no favor to elders.

verses.rationale: Follows the read our form and keeps the unnamed failed ally.
verses.before: Our eyes still failed as we watched for help that was empty. From our watchposts we watched for a nation that could not save.
verses.after: Still our eyes failed, watching in vain for help. From our lookout we kept watching for a nation that could not save.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our eyes still failed as we watched for help that was empty. From our watchposts we watched for a nation that could not save.

verses.rationale: Preserves hunted movement and repeated finality.
verses.before: They hunted our steps so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near; our days were fulfilled, for our end had come.
verses.after: They hunted our steps, so we could not walk in our squares. Our end drew near; our days were full. Our end had come.
verses.tsw_comparator: They hunted our steps so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near; our days were fulfilled, for our end had come.

verses.rationale: Keeps both terrains and the swift-bird comparison.
verses.before: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the heavens. They chased us upon the mountains and lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
verses.after: Our pursuers were swifter than eagles in the sky. They chased us on the mountains and lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the heavens. They chased us upon the mountains and lay in wait for us in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Preserves royal anointed vocabulary, breath/shade images, and the people's disappointed hope.
verses.before: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was captured in their pits— the one of whom we said, “Under his shadow we will live among the nations.”
verses.after: The breath of our nostrils, the **LORD**'s anointed, was caught in their pits— the one of whom we said, “In his shade we will live among the nations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was captured in their pits— the one of whom we said, “Under his shadow we will live among the nations.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the bitter summons, named land, and exposure without softening humiliation.
verses.before: Rejoice and be glad, daughter Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. The cup will pass to you also; you will become drunk and expose yourself.
verses.after: Rejoice and be glad, daughter Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz! The cup will pass to you too; you will become drunk and strip yourself bare.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice and be glad, daughter Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. The cup will pass to you also; you will become drunk and expose yourself.

verses.rationale: Retains contrasting futures and guilt/punishment range rather than harmonizing with the unresolved ending.
verses.before: Your guilt is completed, daughter Zion; he will not continue to exile you. He will attend to your guilt, daughter Edom; he will uncover your sins.
verses.after: Your punishment is complete, daughter Zion; he will not send you into exile again. But he will call your guilt to account, daughter Edom; he will expose your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your guilt is completed, daughter Zion; he will not continue to exile you. He will attend to your guilt, daughter Edom; he will uncover your sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps the communal opening petition and two seeing verbs.
verses.before: Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our reproach.
verses.after: Remember, **LORD**, what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our reproach.

verses.rationale: Preserves inheritance and houses as parallel losses.
verses.before: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
verses.after: Our inheritance has passed to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.

verses.rationale: Retains the comparative like for mothers and explicit fatherlessness.
verses.before: We have become orphans, with no father; our mothers are like widows.
verses.after: We have become orphans, fatherless; our mothers are like widows.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have become orphans, with no father; our mothers are like widows.

verses.rationale: Keeps ownership contrasted with purchase of necessities.
verses.before: We drink our own water for silver; our wood comes to us at a price.
verses.after: We pay silver to drink our own water; we must buy our own wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: We drink our own water for silver; our wood comes to us at a price.

verses.rationale: Preserves the neck image and denied relief, noting compressed syntax.
verses.before: We are pursued at our necks; we are weary, and no rest is given to us.
verses.after: Our pursuers are at our necks. We are exhausted and allowed no rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: We are pursued at our necks; we are weary, and no rest is given to us.

verses.rationale: Keeps the submission gesture, both nations, and hunger motive.
verses.before: We gave the hand to Egypt and to Assyria to be satisfied with bread.
verses.after: We gave our hand to Egypt, to Assyria, to get enough bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: We gave the hand to Egypt and to Assyria to be satisfied with bread.

verses.rationale: Preserves inherited burden without explaining away the protest or harmonizing it with verse 16.
verses.before: Our ancestors sinned; they are no more, and we bear their guilt.
verses.after: Our ancestors sinned and are no more; we bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our ancestors sinned; they are no more, and we bear their guilt.

verses.rationale: Retains the social-status reversal and absent rescuer.
verses.before: Servants rule over us; there is no one to tear us away from their hand.
verses.after: Slaves rule over us; no one rescues us from their hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Servants rule over us; there is no one to tear us away from their hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps danger tied to gathering food, with no invented perpetrators.
verses.before: At the risk of our lives we bring in our bread because of the sword in the wilderness.
verses.after: We risk our lives to bring in bread because of the sword in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the risk of our lives we bring in our bread because of the sword in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the heat comparison and famine's physical effect.
verses.before: Our skin burns like an oven because of the scorching heat of famine.
verses.after: Our skin burns like an oven from hunger's scorching heat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our skin burns like an oven because of the scorching heat of famine.

verses.rationale: Makes sexual violence explicit while retaining the specific groups and locations.
verses.before: Women in Zion were violated, young women in the cities of Judah.
verses.after: They raped women in Zion, virgins in Judah's towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Women in Zion were violated, young women in the cities of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily hanging reading and notes the alternative agency construal.
verses.before: Princes were hung up by their hands; the faces of elders were not honored.
verses.after: Officials were hung by their hands; elders were shown no respect.
verses.tsw_comparator: Princes were hung up by their hands; the faces of elders were not honored.

verses.rationale: Retains forced labor and distinct age groups, with millwork alternative noted.
verses.before: Young men carry millstones, and boys stumble under loads of wood.
verses.after: Young men carry millstones; boys stumble under loads of wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Young men carry millstones, and boys stumble under loads of wood.

verses.rationale: Keeps loss of civic life and song in parallel.
verses.before: Elders have ceased from the gate, and young men from their music.
verses.after: Elders have left the city gate; young men have stopped their music.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elders have ceased from the gate, and young men from their music.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversal of embodied celebration.
verses.before: The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
verses.after: Joy has left our hearts; our dancing has turned to mourning.
verses.tsw_comparator: The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal confession beside earlier inherited-guilt complaint.
verses.before: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
verses.after: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
verses.tsw_comparator: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!

verses.rationale: Preserves the forward-pointing explanation across labels.
verses.before: Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes grow dim:
verses.after: For this our hearts are sick; for these things our eyes grow dim:
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes grow dim:

verses.rationale: Keeps the named place and animal presence without substituting a generic ruin.
verses.before: because Mount Zion is desolate; foxes wander over it.
verses.after: Mount Zion lies desolate, and foxes walk over it.
verses.tsw_comparator: because Mount Zion is desolate; foxes wander over it.

verses.rationale: Retains the turn to enduring kingship without making it the book's resolution.
verses.before: But you, O LORD, remain forever; your throne is from generation to generation.
verses.after: But you, **LORD**, sit enthroned forever; your throne endures from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O LORD, remain forever; your throne is from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unanswered accusation and two time expressions.
verses.before: Why do you forget us forever? Why do you abandon us for so many days?
verses.after: Why do you forget us forever, forsake us for so many days?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you forget us forever? Why do you abandon us for so many days?

verses.rationale: Follows the read return form and leaves the sentence open to the last verse.
verses.before: Turn us back to you, O LORD, and we will return. Renew our days as of old—
verses.after: Bring us back to you, **LORD**, and we will return. Renew our days as they were long ago—
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn us back to you, O LORD, and we will return. Renew our days as of old—

verses.rationale: Preserves the unresolved conditional ending, with the stronger assertion alternative in a note.
verses.before: unless you have utterly rejected us and are exceedingly angry with us.
verses.after: unless you have utterly rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
verses.tsw_comparator: unless you have utterly rejected us and are exceedingly angry with us.

comparative_references.scope: All 154 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
